title: Classification of Living Things (KS2)
subject: Science
strapline: Sorting living things into groups using their features.
facts: Living things are classified (sorted) into groups based on shared features.
The big groups of animals are vertebrates (with a backbone) and invertebrates (without one).
Vertebrates split into five groups: mammals, birds, fish, reptiles and amphibians.
Invertebrates include insects, spiders, snails, worms and crabs.
Plants can be grouped as flowering and non-flowering (such as ferns and mosses).
A classification key asks yes/no questions to identify a living thing step by step.
Scientists group living things to study them and understand how they are related.

quick_quiz.q: What is the difference between a vertebrate and an invertebrate?
quick_quiz.a: a vertebrate has a backbone; an invertebrate does not

quick_quiz.q: Which vertebrate group has moist skin and lives in water and on land?
What does a classification key use to identify a thing?

teacher_tips: Build a branching key from real minibeasts collected outdoors.
Challenge misconceptions: a whale is a mammal, a spider is not an insect.
Sort, then justify — the reasoning matters more than the label.
